author: ojiudezue
title: Room AI rules, chaining and music following: fix and ship on, no shadow mode; observability and room memory instead of approve/undo
summary: Root causes found: rule parsing always failed (HTTP 500, OpenAI rejects the object selector schema; fix is the proven JSON-text pattern); music following's confidence gate measured dwell time, so anyone who stayed >60 s scored 0.5 and was skipped; join leader inverted; MA transfer schema wrong. Plans rewritten for day-1 delivery with fast-bounce safety, primary vs bonus players (Sonos leads in master, tablets are a bonus), decision logs, reversal-based accuracy sensors and room memory episodes.
why: My audit recommended retiring AI rules and a trust ladder (shadow, offer, undo). Operator reversed both: the features are unused because they were never trustworthy, 'the entire point is to build it so I can trust it', and staged rollouts are 'where our features die'. Music following is key to personalization.
implications: Approve/undo card parked with a reversal-rate trigger; its useful parts (digest lines, implicit reversal detection as accuracy and preference signal) fold into the two plans. Overnight agent may build both to review; never deploys.

alternatives_considered.option: Retire AI rules (one rule, never parsed)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: operator: not exercised because not trusted, not because not wanted

alternatives_considered.option: Trust ladder with shadow and offer stages
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: delays and staged rollouts are where features die

revisit_trigger: If the reversal-based accuracy sensor shows people correcting music following or a rule often (>10% within 2 min over 7 days), reopen the approve/undo card.
